# TimeParseError

Why text could not be read as a calendar value.

```rux
pub variant TimeParseError {
    InvalidSyntax(uint),
    InvalidMonth(uint),
    NonexistentDay(uint),
    InvalidTime(uint),
    ExcessiveFraction(uint),
    InvalidOffset(uint)
}
```

Failure-only: every case is a failure, and each carries the zero-based UTF-8 byte offset into the text where it
was found. Success is `Result::Success`.
Copy, carrying one offset.

## Cases

| Name                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InvalidSyntax(uint)`     | The text does not have the shape required: a missing separator, a non-digit where a digit belongs, text after the value, or input that stops early. The offset is where the shape stopped matching, which is the text's length when it ran out. |
| `InvalidMonth(uint)`      | A well-formed two-digit month naming no month. The offset is the first of its digits.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `NonexistentDay(uint)`    | A well-formed day that the month does not have, such as the thirtieth of February. The offset is the first of its digits.                                                                                                                       |
| `InvalidTime(uint)`       | A well-formed hour, minute or second outside its range. The offset is the first digit of the offending field. Second 60 is not here: it is the leap second, and it folds rather than failing.                                                   |
| `ExcessiveFraction(uint)` | More fraction digits than a nanosecond can hold. The offset is the first digit that could not be kept.                                                                                                                                          |
| `InvalidOffset(uint)`     | A well-formed offset outside what an offset may be. The offset is the sign that opened it.                                                                                                                                                      |

## Implements ParseFailure

`TimeParseError` conforms to `ParseFailure`.

<h3 id="offset"><code>Offset</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Offset(self: &TimeParseError) -> uint
```

Where in the input the failure was found.
Borrows the error. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the zero-based UTF-8 byte offset, which is the text's length at end of input
